title: Remittance costs remain high in 2026
discussion_signal: The post interprets remittance costs as a consumer and infrastructure problem: fees, foreign-exchange margins, corridor economics, interoperability, and settlement speed determine how much money reaches families. It highlights a gap between available technology and its uneven deployment across corridors.
linked_research_question: How do payment infrastructure, market power, and regulatory interoperability shape the cost and reliability of cross-border family support?
limits: Professional interpretation of World Bank data
The post does not provide corridor-level validation beyond the cited summary
LinkedIn discussion is not a representative remittance-user sample
